name: Jade Quinn

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am from the independent Work Futures Panel, and this conversation is confidential. What does an ordinary day in your office look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I unlock the accounts cabinet, review returns and tax schedules, and ask juniors where a figure came from before I sign. I like teaching someone how to trace a wrong claim; I dislike the rush to send a tidy PDF before the evidence is ready. I am 43, a senior accountant with a master’s degree and chartered accountancy qualification, and I have never used an AI tool at work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A plateau sounds like the work I know, with a few new buttons at the edges. I still want a paper trail for every tax adjustment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team that a quick draft is useful only when someone can defend the figures. Our clients pay us to explain them, not to decorate a return.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I never use AI tools, and I do not intend to put private client records into one on a whim. My husband Tom repairs electrical systems; his pay and mine cover the mortgage, and we have about four months saved.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would carry on reviewing the tax returns and ask our manager Etta to keep the paper source checklist beside the new software. I would take one corrected account to the next team meeting to show why that checklist matters.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about ordinary bills, not frightened of this little bit of automation. Four months of savings sounds generous until the school roof bill and the mortgage arrive together.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What is one figure you would still check yourself?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: One client tried to claim a van that was mostly family use, and the original mileage book settled the question. I want the mileage book on the desk when a draft says the van claim is fine.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who can decide about that checklist?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Etta can approve a checklist, but I cannot order the whole office around. I would show the van example once, then keep my own signed files sound while the firm still pays me.

say: I would say **quick drafts** still need a person who can defend the figures.
I would ask to keep the **source checklist** beside any new software.
think: I have never used **AI tools** with client records and would need a proper reason to start.
Our **four month reserve** is smaller than it sounds against the mortgage and school bills.
do: Keep reviewing **signed tax returns** against paper source records while my paid work lasts.
Show Etta the **corrected van account** at the next team meeting and ask to retain the paper checklist.
feel: **Uneasy** about ordinary household bills, though the plateau leaves my role steady.
S0.quote: I want the mileage book on the desk when a draft says the van claim is fine.
fieldNote: Jade anchors the **paper checklist** in a disputed van claim, giving her preference for familiar records a concrete client reason.
She is a **senior reviewer** who can propose a process to Etta but cannot set policy for the whole firm.

steps.text: Keep reviewing paid tax returns against original mileage books
Show corrected van account at next meeting and request paper checklist

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If software writes and checks most returns, I expect the junior desks will be the first to empty. I do not like calling that efficiency without saying who loses a wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell our professional association that the firm should say who signs AI prepared accounts and who pays when they are wrong. I would raise that question in its next members meeting.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At our firm, some of my senior checking could also be folded into one screen, and my own paid hours may fall. Tom’s electrical work is useful, but I will not pretend one wage safely covers our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would attend the association meeting and press for a clear liability rule, then ask Etta for paid time to shadow our human tax appeal specialist on two live cases. If she gives assigned supervised hours, I will learn the appeals process; if not, I will keep current paid returns while available and read free appeal decisions at home.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am anxious because the change reaches the paid work under my own hand. I can learn a new part of accounting, but I need an employer to make room for it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Whose work would you learn from?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The specialist is Mabel, and she usually explains why a late appeal is still valid. Two supervised tax appeal cases would teach me more than a glossy course advert.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you do that training on unpaid time?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would not take unpaid leave for the shadowing or put a live appeal on my own desk. Etta would need to assign the cases and paid time, and Mabel would supervise the work.

say: I would ask the **association** who signs AI prepared accounts and carries liability.
I would say empty **junior desks** are lost wages, not just efficiency.
think: My own **senior hours** could shrink even before the firm dismisses anyone.
Tom’s electrical wage alone is a risky base for our **mortgage**.
do: Attend the **association meeting** to press for a clear liability rule.
Learn appeals on **two live cases** only with Etta assigned paid time and Mabel supervising; otherwise read free decisions.
Keep **assigned paid returns** if Etta refuses shadowing, while the firm still offers that work.
feel: **Anxious** about fewer paid hours, with a supervised route to learn.
S1.quote: Two supervised tax appeal cases would teach me more than a glossy course advert.
fieldNote: Her **association question** reflects a practical concern about signatures and liability, rather than faith that software is harmless.
Appeal learning depends on **assigned paid time** and Mabel supervising; free decisions and current paid returns are her fallback.

steps.text: Ask association members who signs AI prepared accounts
Shadow Mabel on two appeals if Etta assigns supervised paid hours
Otherwise read free decisions while assigned paid returns remain

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Full AGI in 2028 would reach our return desks before those 2031 robots have any role here. I would tell colleagues we need actual job and pay dates from Etta.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say in the association that a client should know whether a human checked the return. I would not say a rule can save every accountant’s wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect most of my paid checking hours to disappear within the first year of AGI. Four months of bills in savings is not enough if Tom’s electrical wages alone carry the mortgage and two children.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would stop the children’s extra weekend club at the next term and keep that fee in the household account for bills. If Etta cuts my job after 2028, I will seek posted school bursar roles with written pay, hours and start date that cover the mortgage and fit school pickup; until then I will keep only paid files actually assigned.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed about our own wages, and I have already started counting the months. I can make a plan, but I cannot make a vacancy appear.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the children notice first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The club cost is real, but I would explain to the children that it is a temporary cut and keep their library afternoons. I would not ask Tom to take dangerous extra electrical shifts to hide the gap.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why a school bursar role?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I know a school bursar handles fee records and budgets, which I can do. I will apply only to advertised openings; a friendly chat with a headteacher is not an offer. There are some similar accounting jobs nearby, though a bursar opening still has to be advertised.

say: I would ask Etta for **job dates** because accounting desks face AGI in 2028.
I would ask clients to be told whether a **human checked** their returns.
think: I expect most of my **paid checking hours** to vanish in AGI’s first year.
Our **four month reserve** cannot replace my wage beside a mortgage and two children.
do: Cancel the children’s **weekend club** next term and retain its fee for bills.
After job loss, apply for **posted bursar work** only with written pay, hours and start date fitting mortgage and pickup.
Keep **paid tax files** only while Etta still assigns them before any dismissal.
feel: **Alarmed** about expected income loss, though still able to plan.
S2.quote: I can make a plan, but I cannot make a vacancy appear.
fieldNote: Her **children’s club** is the first named household cut, with library afternoons preserved as a free substitute.
The **bursar search** starts after actual job loss and depends on a posted vacancy plus written household fitting terms.

steps.text: Cancel children’s weekend club next term and keep fee for bills
Keep assigned paid returns only while the firm offers them
After job loss, seek posted bursar role with written mortgage covering pay, pickup hours and start

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years before 2031 is enough time to learn a different slice of accounts if the firm gives me real cases. It does not mean I suddenly trust an AI answer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Etta that we need an appeals rota with supervised places, not a slide about future skills. Tax disputes still need records that can be shown to a client.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think standard returns may go by 2031, even if I become good at appeals. A longer runway lets Tom and me plan the mortgage from our actual wages instead of assuming I will always be employed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Etta for one paid supervised appeal each quarter and work the assigned cases with Mabel, if the firm agrees. If she refuses, I will practise on free published cases after supper while I continue current paid returns only while offered. In the first year after 2031, I would keep only paid appeals or returns the firm still assigns, and use our reserve for bills if those hours end.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am anxious, though I have more time to learn and adjust than with 2028. The fear is still about my wage, not about learning a new form.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why do you need a real case?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: An appeal has an opening letter, evidence and a deadline, so a real assigned case matters. I will not put a client’s deadline at risk by practising unsupervised.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you pay for training yourself?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, I would not use our four month reserve to buy a course. If Etta cannot give paid supervised time, I will use free published cases at home while current paid returns last.

say: I would ask for **supervised appeals** with real cases, not a future skills slide.
I would keep **client evidence** and deadlines visible in each dispute.
think: Standard returns may vanish by **2031** despite my appeal experience.
Our **mortgage plan** must use wages we actually receive.
do: Learn one **paid supervised appeal** each quarter if Etta assigns Mabel and cases.
If refused, practise **free published cases** after supper while current paid returns remain.
Keep **offered paid appeals** or returns after 2031; use the reserve for bills if those hours end.
feel: **Anxious** about my wage, with time to practise carefully.
S3.quote: I will not put a client’s deadline at risk by practising unsupervised.
fieldNote: Her desired **quarterly case** is a concrete learning cadence gated by firm assignment, paid hours and supervision.
She refuses to spend the **four month reserve** on course fees and will practise only on free cases if denied.

steps.text: Work quarterly assigned appeals with Mabel in paid supervised time if Etta agrees
Otherwise practise free cases while current paid returns remain
Keep offered paid files after 2031; use reserve for bills when paid hours end

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years before 2036 sounds like breathing space, but our children will be older then and the mortgage will still send a bill. The desk changes in 2036, not when robots arrive in 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team to keep a human signature on work we do now. I would also ask Etta to publish the pay and hours of any future client adviser post before telling staff to train for it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could stay in a senior role until 2036 and still have my contract reduced after AGI. I will not ask my children to fund my old age because I was too proud to read a job notice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep preparing assigned paid returns and, if Etta offers paid supervised appeals, take one case each quarter with Mabel. After 2036, if my contract shrinks, I would apply for a posted client adviser vacancy only with written pay, start date and hours that cover the mortgage and allow pickup until the children finish school.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy now and would be anxious if my contract actually shrank. A decade lets me be careful without pretending the office is permanent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if Etta offers no appeal cases?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If Etta offers no supervised paid cases, I will work through free appeal decisions while the present salary lasts. I will not turn our mortgage reserve into an unpaid training fund.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you want your children to learn?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Tom and I will show the children how to read pay and hours in an offer when they are older. I want them to know how work decisions are made, not to carry mine.

say: I would ask Etta to publish **adviser pay and hours** before asking staff to train for it.
I would keep a **human signature** on the work we still do.
think: A long tenure may not prevent **contract cuts** after 2036.
I will not ask my **children** to cover my retirement if work shrinks.
do: Keep **paid returns** while assigned and learn quarterly appeals only if Etta grants Mabel-supervised paid time.
After 2036 contract cuts, seek a **posted adviser role** with written mortgage covering pay, start date and suitable hours.
Study **free appeal decisions** if Etta offers no supervised paid cases, while current salary lasts.
feel: **Uneasy** now, with future anxiety if paid contracts fall.
S4.quote: I will not ask my children to fund my old age because I was too proud to read a job notice.
fieldNote: The **2036 desk date** matters to Jade more than the later arrival of robots because her own work is thinking work.
Current **paid files** remain conditional, as do supervised learning and any later adviser move with written terms.

steps.text: Keep assigned paid returns while the firm offers them
Take quarterly Mabel-supervised paid appeals if Etta assigns; otherwise study free decisions
After 2036 cuts, seek posted adviser job with written mortgage covering pay, start and pickup hours

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: The 2028 AGI picture worries me most because our own wages could drop before we can change the mortgage. A posted paid job with real hours, and Etta giving us supervised appeal work now, would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask whether I would miss the juniors. I would miss the moment a junior accountant sees why a client record matters more than a perfect looking draft.

headlineQuote: I would miss the moment a junior accountant sees why a client record matters more than a perfect looking draft.
portrait: Jade is a **43 year old** senior accountant with a master’s degree and chartered qualification who enjoys teaching juniors to trace claims.
She has **never used AI** at work and insists on source records before signing any client return.
Tom’s electrical wages, two school children, a mortgage and **four months saved** make the risk to her own pay immediate.
She seeks **supervised appeals** on paid time, uses free cases if refused, and requires written terms for a later job.
biggestWorry: The **2028 AGI** picture could remove most of her paid checking hours before the mortgage adjusts.
whatWouldHelp: A **posted paid role** with real hours and Etta assigning supervised appeals now would help.
